headline.headline: HART ERUPTS FOR 26, KNICKS ONE FOOT IN NBA FINALS
headline.deck: Brunson adds 19 points and 14 assists as New York goes up 2-0 on Cleveland
headline.body:
NEW YORK -- Josh Hart has spent his career doing the unglamorous work, the rebounds nobody boxes out for, the loose balls nobody dives for. On Thursday night at Madison Square Garden, he did something glamorous. Hart scored a playoff career-high 26 points and the New York Knicks dismantled the Cleveland Cavaliers 109-93, seizing a 2-0 series lead in the Eastern Conference Semifinals and moving to within two victories of the franchise's first NBA Finals appearance in a generation.

Jalen Brunson orchestrated the offense with 19 points and 14 assists, running the Knicks' half-court sets with the patience of a point guard twice his experience. Cleveland had no answer for the combination, and the Cavaliers find themselves staring at a near-impossible deficit, with Games 3 and 4 now set to be played on the road in a Garden that has turned hostile and loud.

The Knicks have now won nine consecutive games, a run that has swept aside every obstacle the Eastern Conference has placed in front of them. New York, a city that spent decades watching its basketball franchise wander through mediocrity, is starting to believe this group is different. Two more wins, and the Garden faithful will have the Finals appearance they have waited for since 1999.

secondary.headline: CANADIENS TORCH HURRICANES IN GAME 1 OF EASTERN FINAL
secondary.deck: Montreal pots four goals in the first period and coasts to a 6-2 rout in Carolina
secondary.body:
RALEIGH -- The Montreal Canadiens did not wait to make their statement. Pouring in four first-period goals, the Canadiens buried the Carolina Hurricanes 6-2 in Game 1 of the Eastern Conference Final on Thursday, putting the hockey world on notice that the youngest team remaining in the Stanley Cup playoffs intends to make this a short series.

Carolina, which entered the second round as one of the favorites in the Eastern bracket, was completely undone by the early onslaught and never recovered. The Hurricanes managed just two goals against a Montreal club that has been growing more dangerous with each passing round. Game 2 remains in Raleigh, and the Hurricanes will need to solve the Canadiens' pace and physicality before this series shifts north to Bell Centre.

secondary.headline: BLUE JAYS BLANK YANKEES, 2-0, AT PACKED BRONX
secondary.deck: Toronto scores in the first and seventh, holds New York hitless in the clutch before 40,249
secondary.body:
NEW YORK -- Before 40,249 fans at Yankee Stadium, the largest crowd of Thursday's baseball slate, the Toronto Blue Jays handed New York a 2-0 shutout defeat that was quiet, efficient, and entirely one-sided. Toronto plated a run in the first inning and another in the seventh, and the Yankees could not string together an answer in any of their nine turns at the plate. Andres Gimenez was hit by a pitch from Cruz in the contest's subplot of frustration for New York.

The Blue Jays' pitching held firm through nine innings, keeping the Yankees off the board in the Bronx for a complete-game effort in terms of run prevention. Toronto has been building toward exactly this kind of performance, and a road win at Yankee Stadium against a divisional rival carries weight in the American League East standings.

secondary.headline: STAFFORD STAYS A RAM: $55M EXTENSION LOCKS UP REIGNING MVP
secondary.deck: Matthew Stafford signs one-year, $55 million deal to remain in Los Angeles after Super Bowl LX title run
secondary.body:
LOS ANGELES -- Matthew Stafford is not going anywhere. The reigning NFL Most Valuable Player and Los Angeles Rams quarterback agreed to a one-year, $55 million contract extension, sources confirmed Thursday, ensuring that the quarterback who led the Rams through a championship run capped by Super Bowl LX in February will be under center when the 2026 season kicks off in September.

At $55 million for a single year, the deal ranks among the richest single-season quarterback contracts in league history and reflects what the Rams believe Stafford is worth at the peak of his powers. Los Angeles made its position clear: there was no offseason search, no open competition, no leverage play. The team that won the Lombardi Trophy in February intends to run it back with the same man under center.

column.headline: THE GARDEN IS ALIVE, AND THE KNICKS ARE FOR REAL
column.body:
There comes a point in every surprising playoff run when you stop calling it a surprise. The New York Knicks have won nine games in a row. Josh Hart just put up 26 points on a night when Jalen Brunson handed out 14 assists. The Cleveland Cavaliers, a team that won 50-plus games this season, left Madison Square Garden looking like they had been outclassed at every position. At some point, the rest of the league needs to stop treating New York as an interesting story and start treating the Knicks as a genuine threat to win the title.

Two wins from the NBA Finals. That is where these Knicks stand on the morning of May 22, 2026. The franchise has not been to the Finals since Allan Houston's shot bounced in off the back of the rim against Miami in 1999. An entire generation of New York basketball fans has grown up knowing only disappointment. This group, built on toughness and collective will rather than superstar hierarchy, is three rounds deep and showing no signs of slowing down. Believe it.

story.headline: ATHLETICS RALLY FROM TWO DOWN TO STUN ANGELS IN TEN
story.deck: Oakland erases early deficit, walks off in extras behind Fermin
story.body:
ANAHEIM — The Athletics spotted the Los Angeles Angels two runs in the first inning Thursday night and then went quiet for four and a half innings before mounting a comeback that ended in the tenth, a 3-2 road victory that required every one of the 25,848 fans in attendance to earn their money's worth.

Oakland chipped away with single runs in the sixth and seventh innings to tie the game at 2-2, then pushed across the winning run in the tenth against an Angel bullpen that had held firm for most of the night. Reliever Fermin earned the win. Zach Gelof, Mason Bolte, and Darell Hernaiz each contributed stolen bases in a game that saw the Athletics strand a remarkable 22 runners on base, a testament to how hard Oakland worked to keep the rally alive.

Schanuel hit his fourth home run of the season for the Angels, and Langeliers added a double for Oakland's offense. The Athletics left 22 runners stranded compared to 10 for the Angels, meaning the comeback required sustained pressure across multiple innings before the decisive run finally crossed the plate in extras.

story.headline: KNICKS SEIZE COMMANDING 2-0 SERIES LEAD OVER CAVALIERS
story.deck: New York rolls past Cleveland 109-93, pushing Cavs to the brink in Eastern Conference Finals
story.body:
NEW YORK — The New York Knicks have put the Cleveland Cavaliers in a desperate position, dispatching them 109-93 at Madison Square Garden on Thursday night to claim a 2-0 lead in the Eastern Conference Finals. The Knicks, third seed in the East at 53-29, controlled the contest with consistent force, outpacing the fourth-seeded Cavaliers across all four quarters and never allowing Cleveland a sustained run to threaten the outcome.

Josh Hart, one of New York's relentless engines off the bench, made clear after the final buzzer that the Knicks are not about to ease off. 'We can't be happy' being up 2-0, Hart told reporters, signaling that the locker room views the series as far from finished business. That edge has defined a New York squad that rode a 53-win regular season and now looks every bit the team capable of a deep postseason run.

For Cleveland, the deficit is stark and the math is unforgiving. No team in NBA history has overcome a 3-0 series deficit, meaning the Cavaliers must win Game 3 at home on Saturday simply to stay alive in a meaningful sense. Despite the double-digit loss, Cavs players insisted the task ahead is not undaunting, pointing to competitive stretches in Game 2 as reason for confidence. The series shifts to Cleveland for Game 3, where the Cavaliers will face an elimination pressure that arrives earlier than anyone in northeast Ohio had hoped.

story.headline: CANADIENS POUR IN FOUR FIRST-PERIOD GOALS, ROUT HURRICANES 6-2 IN GAME 1 OF EASTERN CONFERENCE FINAL
story.deck: Montreal's fast start leaves Carolina reeling after longest postseason break in the playoffs.
story.body:
RALEIGH — The Montreal Canadiens wasted no time making Carolina pay for its extended rest. The Canadiens exploded for four first-period goals against a slow-starting Hurricanes squad, setting the tone early and never letting up in a dominant 6-2 victory Thursday night to open the Eastern Conference Final. Montreal, fresh off back-to-back road Game 7 victories, carried that momentum straight into PNC Arena.

Star defenseman Jaccob Slavin stepped forward after the final buzzer and publicly shouldered the blame for Carolina's uncharacteristic defensive collapse. The Hurricanes, who posted a 53-22-7 record during the regular season and entered the series as the stronger team on paper, looked nothing like that squad in a first period that unraveled almost immediately. Carolina's vaunted defensive structure, the backbone of the organization's identity, simply was not there when the puck dropped.

Montreal now holds a 1-0 series lead heading into Game 2, with the Canadiens' 48-24-10 regular-season mark belying just how dangerous this team has become in the postseason. Carolina will need a dramatic turnaround to avoid falling into a two-game hole at home. Game 2 is Saturday night in Raleigh.

story.headline: QUARTERBACK CAROUSEL SPINS AS TEAMS RETOOL FOR 2026 CAMPAIGN
story.deck: Several franchises are reshaping their rosters this spring with bold moves at signal-caller.
story.body:
The NFL offseason has erupted into a frenzy of quarterback movement this May, with teams that stumbled through the 2025 season now making aggressive plays to secure their franchise cornerstones before training camps open in late July. The Cleveland Browns, desperate to escape another lost season, restructured their roster around newly acquired veteran passer Sam Darnold, shipping two second-round picks to the Minnesota Vikings in a blockbuster deal that sent shockwaves through league front offices. Meanwhile, the Las Vegas Raiders formally released Gardner Minshew, clearing roughly $18 million in cap space and signaling a full organizational rebuild under first-year head coach Mike Vrabel.

The 2026 NFL Draft, held last month in Green Bay, produced its share of immediate controversy. Tennessee quarterback Caleb Hutchinson, the consensus top prospect heading into draft weekend, slipped to fifth overall after three teams traded away their picks rather than absorb his reported contract demands. The Carolina Panthers, picking second, instead grabbed Oregon edge rusher DeShawn Briggs, a move that drew praise from scouts who called Briggs the most physically gifted pass rusher to enter the league since Myles Garrett arrived in Cleveland nearly a decade ago.

Around the rest of the league, the New England Patriots continued their patient rebuild under coordinator-turned-head-coach Jerod Mayo, locking up young wide receiver Kayshon Boutte to a four-year extension worth $64 million. The Dallas Cowboys, fresh off a second-round playoff exit in February, restructured Dak Prescott's contract yet again, buying the franchise another year of financial flexibility while the front office scouts potential long-term successors. Training camps remain roughly ten weeks away, but the deals being cut today will define which rosters contend when the lights come on in September.
